newsitem.title: SUDAN: Water-borne diseases kill dozens in Sudan floods.
newsitem.headline: Water-borne diseases kill dozens in Sudan floods.

text.p: Dozens of Sudanese have died of diarrhoea, gastroenteritis and malaria in the Khartoum shanty town of Mayo because the annual Nile flood has turned the area into a swamp, state television said.
The flooding also destroyed houses and disrupted traffic in the shanty towns of Wad Hussein and Soba, areas inhabited mainly by southerners displaced by civil war, said the report on Monday evening.
Deep pools of water have formed in the areas, providing an excellent breeding ground for mosquitoes and germs.
In Mayo the authorities set up two camps for 1,000 displaced families and are providing drugs and medical services, the official news agency SUNA reported.
The government has sent in earth-moving equipment to dig channels to clear the area of water.
The worst floods this year have been at El Geili north of the capital, where 15 people were killed this month. The state is now building 105 permanent houses there for those who lost homes.
Hydrologists say the floods will be the highest in years because of heavy rain in Ethiopia, the source of the Blue Nile.

State television appealed for donations for flood victims and newspapers said many people had already contributed, including the governors of southern states, companies, other organisations and foreign diplomats.

The Egyptian government sent a planeload of food, tents, blankets and medical supplies on Monday but the Egyptian news agency MENA, in a report published in government newspapers in Cairo, complained that no Sudanese official came to meet it.

Relations between Egypt and Sudan are strained over Egyptian allegations that Sudan shelters its Islamist militants, including three men who tried to kill Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Addis Ababa in June last year.
